fields.sample_size: record review and telephone interviews with purposively sampled councillors and supervisors in various jurisdictions (number not stated); 46 literature items retained from more than 70 journal articles; Auditor-General 2018-19 municipal audit report
fields.effect_estimate: Municipalities cite clean water, jobs and free basic services as the main service-delivery obstacles; 30% of municipalities identified corruption (especially tender awards) as a key cause of service-delivery problems; political interference in municipal administration, deployment of cadres without skills, weak ward committees and perceived collapse of participatory democracy; sanitation is a persistent challenge in rural communities because of missing infrastructure; the Auditor-General reports worsening audit outcomes, with about 60% unqualified audits and only 18 clean audits in 2018-19 and widespread disregard of audit recommendations. Argues the legislative framework is strong but implementation lacks human and financial resources. Qualitative, largely literature and document based; the interview sample is not described.
fields.study_design: qualitative study using record review and telephone interviews (sample not reported) plus literature

evidence_level: Single-study evidence: a qualitative study of South African municipal service delivery (record review and interviews, sample unreported), read in full text 2026-10-04. Corruption cited by 30% of municipalities, political interference and cadre deployment, weak participation and rural sanitation infrastructure gaps; Auditor-General outcomes worsening.

notes: Abstract-level extraction accurate; adds the 30% corruption figure and noted methodological weakness (no sample size). Evidence rests largely on secondary literature.
